SCIAMACHY CO total column data are of sufficient quality for use in the tropics and mid-latitudes for studies of the global distribution and seasonal cycles, but not in the boundary layer over strong emission regions.

SCIAMACHY is an excellent instrument for CO total column observations, but that the IMLM algorithm has to be used with caution, and that the quality of individual SCIAMACHY measurements has to be checked before use.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SCIAMACHY total CO column measurements are suitable for monitoring of the long-term trend of the CO burden in the free troposphere.

SCIAMACHY CO measurements are of sufficient accuracy to provide valuable information on the distribution of the tropospheric CO burden, and that the IMLM algorithm is a good choice for retrieving total CO columns from SCIAMACHY measurements.
SCIAMACHY is a valuable tool for studying the global CO distribution, but it is not yet suitable for quantifying CO emissions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, if individual measurements have good signal-to-nois ratios, SCIAMACHY CO total column measurements can be used to derive the spatial and seasonal distributions of CO in the troposphere over clean areas, while avoiding areas with strong emissions.
SCIAMACHY CO data, when validated, can be used for a wide range of applications, such as CO climatologies, CO trend studies or studies of CO interannual variability.
